earlier_operational_findings.finding: Equinix's contemporaneous SEC filing says its San Jose IBX opened in March 2000; a later SEC filing identifies the San Jose property as its original Silicon Valley IBX, and the current operator page maps SV1 to the exact governed facility.

records.rationale: Equinix SV1 was operational in Santa Clara County more than twenty-one years before NTT SV1 opened. The NTT event is therefore rejected as the county's first operational entry. The broader 74-facility historical inventory has not been proven complete, so the county's true first entry remains unresolved and no treatment date is assigned.

earlier_operational_findings.finding: H5's dated release identifies its exact 2600 West Germann Road facility, reports nearly 40 customers and new deployments, and announces an expansion; its current facility page confirms the governed H5 Phoenix identity.
Digital Realty's 2016 Form 10-K lists 2121 South Price Road as an occupied Phoenix data center, and its current operator page maps that exact address to governed facility PHX15.

records.rationale: Two exact Maricopa County facilities are documented operational before Apple's March 2017 service date. The Apple event is therefore rejected as the county's first operational entry. The broader 55-facility historical inventory has not been proven complete, so the county's true first entry remains unresolved and no treatment date is assigned.

earlier_operational_findings.finding: The exact 1033 Jefferson Street building was converted in part for telecom and data-center use beginning in 2000 and housed Sprint's approximately 100,000-square-foot e|Solutions center in 2001. QTS's SEC property schedule independently maps Atlanta DC1 to a 2006 acquisition year.

An April 2003 industry account identifies 56 Marietta as a carrier-neutral colocation facility with an adjacent enterprise data center, while Digital Realty's current operator record maps the governed ATL13 facility to that exact address.

records.rationale: The October 2006 QTS observation is not Fulton County's first operational entry. The same exact Jefferson Street building hosted a Sprint data center in 2001, and 56 Marietta was operating as a carrier-neutral colocation and data-center complex by April 2003. The broader 13-facility current inventory and historical predecessor inventory have not been proven complete, so the county's true first entry remains unresolved and no treatment date is assigned.

SunGard's signed March 27, 2002 Form 10-K documents an operating Availability Services MegaCenter in North Bergen and identifies its exact 5851 West Side Avenue facility; Equinix's current NY7 page maps that address to the governed facility. The same filing traces the lease to November 1987, but a lease date does not establish when data-center operations began. Hudson County's complete historical facility inventory and a conclusive search for earlier operations have not been established, so 2002-03-27 is retained only as an operational-no-later-than anchor and no county first-entry treatment date is assigned.

earlier_operational_findings.finding: Switch's September 3, 2008 county filing identifies its existing NAP4 data center at 4495 East Sahara Avenue while describing NAP7 at 7135 South Decatur Boulevard as still under construction.

records.rationale: NAP7 cannot be Clark County's first operational data-center entry. Clark County's September 3, 2008 filing identifies NAP4 at 4495 East Sahara Avenue as an existing Switch data center and NAP7 at 7135 South Decatur Boulevard as a new facility still under construction; Switch places the SUPERNAP/NAP7 debut in 2009. The broader 20-facility current inventory and historical predecessor inventory have not been proven complete, so the county's true first entry remains unresolved and no treatment date is assigned.

earlier_operational_findings.finding: Indiana University's 2003 state record documents an October 24, 2001 reception and tour of the operational Wrubel Computing Center machine room and its recently upgraded IBM SP supercomputer. IU's later facility history identifies Wrubel as the predecessor old center replaced by the 2009 Data Center.

records.rationale: Indiana University's official ceremonies record supplies a November 5, 2009 operational-no-later-than anchor for the new Bloomington Data Center, corroborated by the university's May 2009 capital-project completion record. The candidate cannot be Monroe County's first data-center entry because an IU state record documents the named Wrubel Computing Center machine room and its upgraded operating supercomputer on October 24, 2001, and IU's facility history identifies Wrubel as the predecessor old center. IU's archives trace county computing facilities further back, while the full historical facility inventory has not been established, so the true first entry remains unresolved and no treatment date is assigned.

earlier_operational_findings.canonical_name: 123NET Southfield Data Center at 24700 Northwestern Highway
earlier_operational_findings.finding: 123NET's June 20, 2014 operator release identifies its 24700 Northwestern Highway headquarters as an operating data center and records a recent 15,000-square-foot expansion of data-center space.

records.rationale: EdgeConneX's March 11, 2015 release supplies an operational-no-later-than anchor for its Southfield Edge Data Center; the current DET01 data sheet maps that facility to 21005 Lahser Road, and Southfield's 2012-2013 financial report documents the same address as a vacant shell awaiting complete data-center build-out. DET01 cannot be Oakland County's first entry because 123NET's June 20, 2014 operator release identifies a separate operating and recently expanded data center at 24700 Northwestern Highway. 123NET's current inventory also identifies multiple Southfield facilities, while the complete historical county inventory has not been established, so the true first entry remains unresolved and no treatment date is assigned.

earlier_operational_findings.finding: Digital Realty's SEC property history identifies 350 East Cermak Road as an eight-story data center and Internet gateway created by a complete 1999-2000 renovation, establishing operation no later than 2000.

records.rationale: FiberNet Telecom Group's signed March 28, 2003 Form 10-K supplies an operational-no-later-than anchor for the exact 600 South Federal Street carrier hotel, and Digital Realty's current page maps that address to ORD11. The candidate cannot be Cook County's first data-center entry because Digital Realty's SEC property history states that the separate 350 East Cermak Road building was completely renovated in 1999-2000 to create a data center and Internet gateway. Cook County's 28-facility current canonical inventory and earlier predecessor inventory have not been proven complete, so the county's true first entry remains unresolved and no treatment date is assigned.

earlier_operational_findings.canonical_name: University of Florida Northeast Regional Data Center
earlier_operational_findings.finding: UF's March 31, 2003 administrative record identifies the Northeast Regional Data Center as a large multipurpose computing and network services facility operating continuously, 24 hours a day and 365 days a year.

records.rationale: UFIT's maintained history supplies a year-precision 2012 operational anchor for the exact East Campus Research Computing Center, and UF's 2011 construction announcement establishes that building's data-center and HPC identity. The candidate cannot be Alachua County's first data-center entry because UF's March 31, 2003 administrative record describes the separate Northeast Regional Data Center as a large multipurpose computing facility operating 24/365. The current two-record canonical inventory is co-located at East Campus and does not establish a complete legacy inventory, so the county's true first entry remains unresolved and no treatment date is assigned.

earlier_operational_findings.finding: The University of Maine System's June 8, 2009 report includes a May 14 network status update naming 340 Cumberland as one of Portland's two existing colocation facilities. Maine Connectivity Authority later identifies the exact address as Maine's carrier hotel and names FirstLight among the carriers housed there, corroborating the canonical point's address and operator relationship.

records.rationale: Bangor Daily News supplies a conservative September 28, 2011 operational-no-later-than anchor for the Resilient Tier-V facility at the former Brunswick Naval Air Station; FirstLight's current facility page and MaineDOT's address record establish continuity to the exact mapped building at 14 Resilient Circle. The Brunswick candidate cannot be Cumberland County's first entry because the University of Maine System's June 8, 2009 report identifies 340 Cumberland in Portland as an existing colocation facility. Maine Connectivity Authority's later official application corroborates the exact address as Maine's carrier hotel and names FirstLight among its occupants. The two-record current canonical inventory does not establish a complete historical county inventory, so the true first entry remains unresolved and no treatment date is assigned.

earlier_operational_findings.canonical_name: CoreSite BO1 at 70 Inner Belt Road
earlier_operational_findings.finding: CoreSite's SEC prospectus records the April 11, 2007 acquisition of 70 Innerbelt with operating data-center space, and Somerville's permit history says a December 2007 application expanded an existing 22,667-square-foot colocation data center. CoreSite's current page maps BO1 to the exact address.

records.rationale: Markley's November 23, 2015 operator post supplies an operational-no-later-than anchor for the Lowell facility and states that Phase One had opened with customers already occupying space; Markley's current facility and contact pages establish continuity to the exact mapped building at One Markley Way. The Lowell candidate cannot be Middlesex County's first entry because CoreSite's SEC prospectus identifies 70 Innerbelt in Somerville as operating data-center space when it was acquired on April 11, 2007, and Somerville's permit history independently describes an existing colocation data center at that address later in 2007. CoreSite's current page maps BO1 to 70 Inner Belt Road. The current two-record canonical inventory and the records reviewed do not establish a complete historical county inventory or the original opening date of the Somerville facility, so the true first entry remains unresolved and no treatment date is assigned.
